summary: This is a Mol Labs public hypothesis card (L21) proposing an assumption-kill experiment to test whether Urolithin A (UA) retains lifespan or muscle-function benefits in C. elegans under PINK1/Parkin (pink-1/pdr-1) genetic loss-of-function or equivalent mitophagy block. The document frames the question as: does UA lifespan benefit depend solely on mitophagy (as Ryu 2016 necessity data suggest), or does a residual lifespan phenotype persist under abolished mitophagy-class control? The experiment has NOT been run; the residual-positive outcome is explicitly labeled UNKNOWN.

content_blocks.title: Hypothesis / Claim (L21)
content_blocks.content: On a pre-registered C. elegans panel with UA vs vehicle under pink-1/pdr-1 genetic LOF (or equivalent mitophagy block that abolishes mitophagy-class control benefit) vs mitophagy-intact concurrent controls, the primary question is whether same-panel median lifespan improvement (UA vs vehicle under block) retains ≥50% of the UA vs vehicle median lifespan improvement on mitophagy-intact concurrent controls. This is framed as an 'assumption-kill' / mitophagy-insufficiency test. Residual-positive lifespan or muscle-function H2H under mitophagy block is explicitly labeled UNKNOWN — not invented.

content_blocks.title: Scientific Rationale / Mechanism Sketch
content_blocks.content: Ryu Nat Med (PMID 27400265) shows mitophagy is required for UA-mediated longevity in C. elegans (necessity, inverse of residual). pink-1/dct-1/skn-1 RNAi and pdr-1 mutation abolish/impair lifespan and mobility arms. Huang Parkin silencing + Mdivi-1 blunt UA myocardial protection (residual cardiac contradicted on that panel). Denk Pink1-dependent TSCM and Ambra1/PINK1 cardioprotection necessity are adjacent endpoints, not residual wild-type lifespan/muscle. The card asks whether, once PINK1/Parkin block abolishes mitophagy-class control benefit, UA still retains lifespan phenotype — i.e., lifespan ≠ mere mitophagy-sole-necessity bridge.

content_blocks.title: Prior Art Summary
content_blocks.content:
1. PMID 27400265 (Ryu Nat Med 2016, DOI 10.1038/nm.4132): UA induces mitophagy; extends C. elegans lifespan and mobility; improves rodent muscle; Fig. 3 shows mitophagy required for UA-mediated longevity; pink-1/dct-1/skn-1 RNAi and pdr-1 mutation abolish/impair longevity and mobility arms — NECESSITY (inverse of residual); not residual-positive H2H under mitophagy block.
2. PMID 34117375 (Singh et al. 2022, DOI 10.1038/s41430-021-00950-1): Direct UA supplementation achieves consistent human exposure vs diet/microbiome variability — human exposure/translational prior; ≠ residual under PINK1/Parkin block.
3. PMID 35778837 (D'Ambrosio et al., DOI 10.1111/acel.13662): UA improves mitophagy and mitochondrial health in OA chondrocytes and mouse OA — mitochondrial-health phenotype prior; ≠ residual under mitophagy block.
4. PMID 36351375 (Denk Immunity 2022, DOI 10.1016/j.immuni.2022.09.014): UA-induced TSCM formation depended on Pink1-mediated mitophagy — NECESSITY immune/TSCM ≠ residual lifespan or muscle-function under mitophagy block.
5. Optional: PMID 35655094 and 39725191 (Parkin/Mdivi-1 and Ambra1-PINK1 abolish/blunt UA cardioprotection) — against residual cardiac; out of public prior_art.

content_blocks.title: Proposed Experimental Design
content_blocks.content: Model system: C. elegans (preferred before new rodent muscle or human dosing). Intervention: Urolithin A (UA) vs vehicle. Genetic manipulation: pink-1/pdr-1 genetic LOF (or equivalent chemical mitophagy block that abolishes mitophagy-class control benefit). Controls: mitophagy-intact concurrent controls on the same panel. Primary readout: median lifespan (days), pre-specified α/N. Secondary/optional co-readouts: mobility / muscle-function (not gate). Threshold: block-arm median lifespan improvement (UA vs vehicle under block) retains ≥50% of UA vs vehicle median lifespan improvement on mitophagy-intact concurrent controls. Competing outcomes: block not actually abolishing mitophagy-class control benefit, underpowered strata, or referee-assay mismatch → inconclusive (not refuted). Refute condition: <50% retention when block-not-abolished/underpowered/assay-mismatch artifacts are ruled out.

content_blocks.title: Execution Status and IP
content_blocks.content: Execution status: NOT_RUN. FTO status: UNKNOWN. IP class: mitophagy-insufficiency. Kill cost tier: 1. Time to refute: 4 weeks. Vault hold: no. Status label: NEGATIVE (assumption-kill, polarity negative). The experiment has not been performed; the residual-positive outcome is UNKNOWN and must not be invented.

content_blocks.title: Ablation / Actionable Limitations
content_blocks.content:
1. Do not treat L1–L20 as proving L21 — new parent area urolithin-mitophagy-insufficiency; Ryu/Denk/Parkin-cardiac layers are necessity or adjacent, not residual-positive H2H under mitophagy block; soft-complete empty ≠ demonstrated prediction-failure; do not invent residual.
2. PMID 27400265 NECESSITY constrains residual lifespan/mobility; optional 35655094/39725191 constrain residual cardiac; 36351375/41400574 wrong or disease-context endpoints leave matched residual-positive lifespan/muscle H2H UNKNOWN — PRIOR_ART PARTIAL.
3. L15 ≠ L21; L16 ≠ L21; L17 ≠ L21; L18 ≠ L21; L19 ≠ L21; L20 ≠ L21 (mitophagy/PINK1/Parkin ≠ bulk ATG); NOT SERIES_FROZEN NAD-after-senolysis.
4. Without the block-lock × residual lifespan H2H on the same panel, separate Ryu necessity LITERATURE and Denk/Parkin-cardiac adjacent necessity cannot show lifespan ≠ mere mitophagy-sole-necessity bridge.
5. Without the intact-arm UA vs vehicle median lifespan comparator under the block lock, the card collapses into unmatched necessity framing and loses the mitophagy-insufficiency assumption-kill.

key_findings: Ryu Nat Med 2016 (PMID 27400265) demonstrates NECESSITY: mitophagy is required for UA-mediated longevity in C. elegans; pink-1/dct-1/skn-1 RNAi and pdr-1 mutation abolish/impair lifespan and mobility arms — this is necessity evidence, not residual-positive H2H under mitophagy block.

Residual-positive UA lifespan or muscle-function H2H under PINK1/Parkin genetic or equivalent mitophagy block that abolishes mitophagy-class control is explicitly UNKNOWN (soft-complete Q_resid_tight=0); no such experiment has been run.
The proposed experiment is NOT_RUN; execution status is NOT_RUN and FTO status is UNKNOWN.

The prediction gate is: block-arm median lifespan improvement (UA vs vehicle under block) retains ≥50% of UA vs vehicle median lifespan improvement on mitophagy-intact concurrent controls on the same C. elegans panel.
Denk Immunity 2022 (PMID 36351375) shows UA-induced TSCM formation depends on Pink1-mediated mitophagy — NECESSITY for immune endpoint, not residual lifespan or muscle-function.
Parkin silencing + Mdivi-1 blunt UA myocardial protection (residual cardiac contradicted on that panel); Ambra1/PINK1 cardioprotection necessity are adjacent endpoints.
UA human exposure is achievable via direct supplementation (PMID 34117375), but this is a translational prior unrelated to residual under PINK1/Parkin block.
UA improves mitophagy and mitochondrial health in OA chondrocytes and mouse OA (PMID 35778837) — mitochondrial-health phenotype prior, not residual under mitophagy block.
Kill cost tier = 1; estimated time to refute = 4 weeks (C. elegans lifespan assay); ip_class = mitophagy-insufficiency.
Status label is NEGATIVE (assumption-kill, polarity negative); the card is a research-discussion hypothesis, not a completed experiment.
